newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia winning skin cancer battle - study.
newsitem.headline: Australia winning skin cancer battle - study.

text.p: Australia appears to be winning the battle to contain an epidemic of melanoma, the most dangerous form of skin cancer, according to a report published on Tuesday.

The study, released on the eve of the fourth World Conference on Melanoma, found the steady increase of the cancer has now levelled off among women in New South Wales, the country's most populous state.
While the number of men contracting the cancer was still rising, the incidence in people under 50 had fallen over six years to 1995, it said.
"It's probable we are very near the peak of the epidemic," Professor Bruce Armstrong of the Cancer Control Information Centre told a briefing.

The turnaround follows a high-profile public health campaign, boosted in part by publicity surrounding the depletion of the ozone layer which has led to an increase in harmful ultra-violet radiation over southern Australia.
Armstrong said women had been quicker to respond to the message than men as they were more likely to care for their health and appearance.
Men were also more likely to remain active in sports which kept them out in the sun, such as golf or yachting.

The study also found an increasing incidence of melanoma in people from wealthier areas. "This is almost undoubtedly a consequence of the access that the better-off have to sun-related recreation," Armstrong said.
The four-day conference will examine the latest proposals to counter melanoma, including early diagnosis, new surgical treatments and the effect of attitude on survival rates.
